at intensivere.explanation: "At intensivere" means "to intensify". To say the police search harder, use it with the search: "Politiet intensiverer eftersøgningen" (The police are intensifying the search).

at interessere.explanation: "At interessere" means "to interest". To say a thing interests you, put the thing first: "Fodbold interesserer mig" (Soccer interests me). To say you are interested, use "interesseret" (interested) with "i" (in): "Jeg er interesseret i fodbold" (I am interested in soccer).

at interessere sig for.explanation: "At interessere sig for" means "to be interested in". To say you are interested in something, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg interesserer mig for musik" (I am interested in music). To say a woman is, use "sig" (herself): "Hun interesserer sig for kunst" (She is interested in art). Without "sig" and "for", "at interessere" means "to interest": "Musik interesserer mig" (Music interests me).

at interviewe.explanation: "At interviewe" means "to interview". English speakers should remember the final "e" in the spelling. To say a journalist questions a politician, say: "Journalisten interviewer ministeren" (The journalist interviews the minister).

at introducere.explanation: "At introducere" means "to introduce". To say you bring in something new, say: "Firmaet introducerer en ny telefon" (The company is introducing a new phone). To introduce one person to another, use "at præsentere" (to present) instead: "Må jeg præsentere Anna?" (May I introduce Anna?).

at invadere.explanation: "At invadere" means "to invade". To say an army enters a country, say: "Hæren invaderer landet" (The army is invading the country). To say a place is filled with many people, say: "Turisterne invaderer byen" (The tourists are invading the town).

at investere.explanation: "At investere" means "to invest". To say what you put money into, add "i" (in) after it: "Hun investerer i en lejlighed" (She is investing in a flat). To say you put time into something, say: "Jeg investerer mange timer i projektet" (I am investing many hours in the project).

at invitere.explanation: "At invitere" means "to invite". To invite someone for coffee, add "på" (for) after the person: "Må jeg invitere dig på kaffe?" (May I invite you for coffee?).

at irritere.explanation: "At irritere" means "to irritate". To say a noise annoys you, say: "Larmen irriterer mig" (The noise annoys me). To say you are annoyed, use "irriteret" (annoyed): "Jeg er irriteret" (I am annoyed).

at isolere.explanation: "At isolere" means "to isolate / insulate". To say you insulate a building against cold, say: "Vi isolerer loftet" (We are insulating the attic). To say a person is kept away from others, say: "Patienten bliver isoleret" (The patient is being isolated).

en iagttager.explanation: "En iagttager" means "an observer". It comes from the verb "at iagttage" (to observe): "Jeg iagttager fuglene fra vinduet" (I watch the birds from the window).

en identitet.explanation: "En identitet" means "an identity". To talk about the identity of a country, use "national" (national): "en national identitet" (a national identity).

en idrætshal.explanation: "En idrætshal" means "a sports hall". It is built from "idræt" (sports) and "en hal" (a hall). To say you have the school subject, use "idræt" alone: "Vi har idræt i morgen" (We have PE tomorrow).

en idé.explanation: "En idé" means "an idea". To say you get an idea, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en idé" (I got an idea). To say you have no idea, say: "Jeg aner det ikke" (I have no clue).

en igangsætter.explanation: "En igangsætter" means "an initiator". It comes from "at sætte i gang" (to set something going): "Vi sætter projektet i gang" (We are getting the project started).

en illusion.explanation: "En illusion" means "an illusion". To say you have no false hopes about something, say: "Jeg har ingen illusioner om det" (I have no illusions about it).

en illustration.explanation: "En illustration" means "an illustration". It comes from the verb "at illustrere" (to illustrate): "Tegneren illustrerer bogen" (The artist illustrates the book). To say an example makes a point clear, say: "Det er en god illustration af problemet" (That is a good illustration of the problem).

en implikation.explanation: "En implikation" means "an implication". To ask what a decision leads to, use the plural: "Hvad er implikationerne?" (What are the implications?)

en indbakke.explanation: "En indbakke" means "an inbox". It is built from "ind" (in) and "en bakke" (a tray). "Bakke" also means "hill", as in "Cyklen ruller ned ad bakken" (The bike rolls down the hill).

en indblanding.explanation: "En indblanding" means "an interference". To say someone dislikes others getting involved, say: "Hun bryder sig ikke om andres indblanding" (She does not like other people butting in).

en indbygger.explanation: "En indbygger" means "an inhabitant". To say how many people live in a place, say: "Byen har 50.000 indbyggere" (The town has 50,000 inhabitants).

en inddragelse.explanation: "En inddragelse" means "an involvement". To say people take part in a decision, say: "inddragelse af borgerne" (involving the residents). Do not mix it up with "indblanding" (interference): "Hun bryder sig ikke om andres indblanding" (She does not like other people butting in). To say a license is taken away officially, say: "inddragelse af kørekort" (taking away a driver's license).

en inder.explanation: "En inder" means "an Indian". It comes from the country "Indien" (India). To say food is Indian, use "indisk" (Indian): "indisk mad" (Indian food). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Mange indianere boede i Nordamerika" (Many Native Americans lived in North America).

en inderside.explanation: "En inderside" means "an inside". It is built from "inder" (inner) and "en side" (a side). To say a page number, "side" also means "page": "side 12" (page 12).

en indflydelse.explanation: "En indflydelse" means "an influence". To say you have influence over something, use "at have indflydelse på" (to have influence on): "Jeg har ingen indflydelse på det" (I have no say in it).
